methodology.career_timeline: PRS Legislative Research MP pages, official Sansad/BJP/Congress/Census-of-India profile pages, and mainstream press biography pieces, cross-checked with Wikipedia. Extended back to approximately age 18 where sourced. Any claim about early-life employment, education credentials, or personal history that is self-reported, unverified by an independent record, or actively disputed in the press is explicitly labeled 'allegedly' or flagged with a note on sourcing strength — it is not presented as settled fact.
methodology.criminal_civil_cases: Two tiers: (1) 'declared_affidavit' = sworn ECI election affidavit via MyNeta/ADR, factual and legally self-declared. (2) 'media_allegation' = reported by an established newspaper/wire service, explicitly labeled an allegation, not a proven fact, with current legal status and a case_summary paragraph. Where a specific declared case count could not be confirmed from available search results, that is stated explicitly rather than guessed at or assumed to be zero.
methodology.promises: Sourced from newspaper headline coverage of rallies, manifestos, speeches, or interviews. Lists are most extensive for the most prolific public speakers (Modi, Rahul Gandhi); other MPs get a proportionate, still-sourced set. Where a promise is publicly disputed or fact-checked, both the popular belief and the sourced clarification are included rather than picking a side.
methodology.note: Every entry has a source_url. Nothing here has been inferred or filled in without a citation — where evidence was thin or unconfirmed, that is stated rather than guessed at.

career_timeline.position: Helped his father run a tea stall at Vadnagar railway station, Gujarat (widely repeated biographical claim from Modi's own account and BJP-published biography; independent corroboration is limited to family/townspeople interviews given decades later)

Married Jashodaben Chimanlal Modi in an arranged marriage; the marriage was not publicly acknowledged for over four decades and was first officially disclosed by Modi in his 2014 Lok Sabha election affidavit

Allegedly left home and traveled around India, including stays near the Himalayas and at Belur Math and other ashrams, before returning to Gujarat — this period is self-described in Modi's own authorized accounts/interviews and is not independently documented
career_timeline.source_name: Narendra Modi official biography site / press profiles

career_timeline.position: Became a full-time RSS (Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh) pracharak (organizer)

Reportedly earned a B.A. (Delhi University, external/correspondence) and an M.A. in political science (Gujarat University, 1983) — the authenticity of both degrees has been repeatedly and publicly disputed; this is treated as an allegedly-contested claim, see case_allegations below
RSS deputed him to full-time work with the BJP
Organized BJP's campaign for the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation election
Helped organize L.K. Advani's Somnath-to-Ayodhya Rath Yatra
BJP national secretary / general secretary (organization)
Chief Minister of Gujarat
Prime Minister of India (3rd consecutive term from 2024)

case_allegations.description: No criminal cases declared in 2024 Lok Sabha election affidavit.
case_allegations.case_summary: In his sworn ECI candidacy affidavit for the 2024 Lok Sabha election from Varanasi, Modi declared zero pending or past criminal cases against him.

case_allegations.description: Allegation that as Gujarat CM he bore responsibility for the 2002 Gujarat riots; Zakia Jafri petitioned against the SIT's clean chit to him.
case_allegations.case_summary: Following the February 2002 Gujarat riots, 69 people including former Congress MP Ehsan Jafri were killed in the Gulberg Society massacre in Ahmedabad. Jafri's widow, Zakia Jafri, filed a complaint alleging a 'larger conspiracy' by 63 people including then-CM Modi. A Supreme Court-appointed SIT probed the complaint and, in a February 2012 closure report, found no prosecutable evidence against Modi and the others. Zakia Jafri filed a protest petition challenging that clean chit.
case_allegations.status: cleared — SIT clean chit (2012) upheld by Supreme Court, Zakia Jafri's petition dismissed June 24, 2022

case_allegations.description: Degree-authenticity dispute: AAP leaders publicly questioned whether Modi's B.A./M.A. degrees are genuine; Modi filed a defamation complaint against them.
case_allegations.case_summary: AAP leaders Arvind Kejriwal and Manish Sisodia repeatedly questioned the authenticity of Modi's Delhi University B.A. and Gujarat University M.A. degrees. BJP held a 2016 press conference displaying the degree certificates to rebut the claims. Modi filed a private criminal defamation complaint against Kejriwal and other AAP leaders.
case_allegations.status: Modi's defamation complaint was dismissed by an Ahmedabad court in 2017 for lack of evidence of malicious intent; the underlying degree-authenticity dispute remains unresolved as public back-and-forth

case_allegations.description: 'Snoopgate' (2013): Amit Shah is alleged on leaked recordings to have ordered illegal surveillance on the instructions of a figure referred to only as 'saheb', widely presumed to mean Modi as then-CM.
case_allegations.case_summary: In November 2013, Cobrapost and Gulail published audio recordings in which Amit Shah is heard directing off-the-books surveillance of a young woman referred to as 'Madhuri' in 2009, allegedly on orders from 'saheb'. Modi was not named directly and has not been formally charged; the 'saheb' identification remains a media inference.
case_allegations.status: no criminal case was filed against Modi personally

promises.promise_text: Popularly remembered as: 'Rs 15 lakh will be deposited in every Indian's bank account' (from recovered black money), 2014 campaign.
promises.public_belief_vs_fact: Widely believed and cited as a broken promise; BJP president Amit Shah later called it a political 'jumla'.

promises.promise_text: 'Achhe din aane wale hain' (good days are coming) — general promise of development and an end to corruption.
promises.public_belief_vs_fact: Became the defining, and most-mocked, slogan of the campaign; opposition repeatedly invokes 'where are the achhe din?'

promises.promise_text: Black money stashed abroad (claimed ₹80 lakh crore) recovered within 100 days of taking office.
promises.public_belief_vs_fact: Not fulfilled as stated; only ~₹3,770 crore recovered under the compliance window.

promises.promise_text: Two crore new jobs to be created every year.
promises.public_belief_vs_fact: Widely cited by opposition and economists as unmet.

promises.promise_text: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan — India open-defecation free by October 2, 2019.
promises.public_belief_vs_fact: Government declared India ODF on schedule in 2019; independent surveys disputed completeness.

promises.promise_text: Doubling farmers' income by 2022.
promises.public_belief_vs_fact: Not achieved; NSSO data shows ~21% real growth 2012-13 to 2018-19, well short of doubling.

promises.promise_text: 'Housing for All' by 2022.
promises.public_belief_vs_fact: Large PMAY completion numbers cited by government, but 'zero homeless families' framing not achieved by deadline per independent reporting.

promises.promise_text: Construction of Ram Mandir at Ayodhya — decades-old BJP manifesto commitment.
promises.public_belief_vs_fact: Delivered: foundation laid August 2020, consecration ceremony led by Modi January 2024.

case_allegations.description: 18 criminal cases declared, mostly defamation-related sections.
case_allegations.case_summary: Rahul Gandhi's 2024 affidavit lists 18 pending criminal cases, mostly IPC 499/500 defamation matters from political speeches, filed largely by BJP-affiliated private complainants.
case_allegations.status: mostly pending; see Surat conviction below

case_allegations.description: Surat 'Modi surname' defamation case: convicted, disqualified as MP, conviction stayed by Supreme Court.
case_allegations.case_summary: A 2019 remark ('how come all thieves have Modi as common surname') led BJP MLA Purnesh Modi to file a defamation complaint in Surat. Convicted March 2023, triggering automatic MP disqualification; Supreme Court stayed the conviction August 2023, restoring his seat.
case_allegations.status: conviction stayed; appeal pending in Gujarat courts

case_allegations.description: National Herald case: ED alleges illegal acquisition of Associated Journals Ltd assets via Young Indian.
case_allegations.case_summary: ED alleges Sonia and Rahul Gandhi, holding 76% of Young Indian, acquired Associated Journals' debts/assets (worth over ₹2,000 crore) for ~₹50 lakh in a 2010 transaction, generating ₹142 crore in alleged proceeds of crime.
case_allegations.status: ongoing — chargesheet filed April 2025; Delhi court declined cognisance Dec 2025; ED appealed

case_allegations.description: RSS defamation case (Bhiwandi): sued over a 2014 remark linking RSS to Gandhi's assassination.
case_allegations.case_summary: RSS activist Rajesh Kunte filed a defamation complaint over Gandhi's 2014 remark 'RSS people shot Gandhiji'.

case_allegations.description: Alleged British citizenship: petitioner claims Rahul Gandhi held British citizenship; Allahabad HC ordered an FIR.
case_allegations.case_summary: A petitioner alleged documentary proof of British citizenship. Underlying claim sourced mainly to BJP-affiliated petitioners and right-leaning outlets, with no neutral corroboration found; Allahabad HC directed FIR registration in April 2026.
case_allegations.status: ongoing — not yet adjudicated on the merits
